clue.text: Authorised putting soldier in front of square

parts.note: a man is a soldier in the ranks
square in the sense of old-fashioned, out of date

explanation.surface: An officer approves a soldier's place at the front of a parade square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a parade ground, but it is the slang adjective for old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandated means given official authority or commanded, a synonym for authorised.

clue.text: Drive or other kind of golf shot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the private road leading up to a house
second meaning: the shot played onto the green, as opposed to a drive off the tee

explanation.surface: Choosing between a drive and some other stroke on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a list of golf shots, but 'Drive' is the road to a house, a separate sense from the golfer's drive.
explanation.definitionFit: The road leading to a building is its approach, and in golf an approach is the shot played towards the green.

clue.text: Deal is arranged with people for main treatment?

indicators.note: a deal that is arranged has its terms set in order, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A deal is struck with people to fix the town's water mains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the poetic word for the sea, not a water pipe; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the salt from seawater is treating the main, the old literary name for the ocean.

clue.text: Cutting a new pattern for unisex garment

parts.note: a cutting remark is a tart one: sharp, biting
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A tailor cutting a fresh pattern for clothing either sex can wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' suggests scissors and fabric, but it is the adjective meaning sharp-tongued.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is the checked woollen design of the Scottish kilt and plaid, worn by men and women alike.

clue.text: Beloved daughter hearing organ

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A cherished daughter's ear, perhaps examined by a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear is an adjective for someone loved or cherished.

clue.text: Getting rid of old pass I shredded

indicators.note: something shredded is cut to pieces, so the letters are torn apart and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, to be torn up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone throwing out an expired pass by putting it through the shredder.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposal is the act of throwing something away, a noun matching 'getting rid of'.

clue.text: How one flies extremely close to ground, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: so means very, extremely
low means near the ground

explanation.surface: A description of how a pilot flies when skimming the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of LOW is dropped. 'How one flies' is fair: one, on one's own, flies alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot flying alone, especially a trainee's first unaccompanied flight, is said to fly solo.

clue.text: Settle account, including pound for theatre poster

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: to settle an account is to pay a bill
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Paying a bill that includes a pound for a theatre poster.
explanation.walkthrough: The L goes after the P of PAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A playbill is a printed notice advertising a play and its cast.

clue.text: Vote in unusually polite line — then take part in this?

indicators.note: in tells us the vote mark sits inside the other letters
unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters appear in an abnormal order

parts.note: a voter marks the ballot paper with a cross
taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Cast your vote while queuing politely, then answer the pollster's questions afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: after voting you might be stopped and asked how you voted.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit poll surveys voters as they leave the polling station, so one takes part after voting.

clue.text: Piece of music band advertise endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the word drops its last letter

parts.note: a ring is a band, and a ring is shaped like O
to push a product is to promote it

explanation.surface: A band advertising one of their pieces without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is a ring, the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical work, as in the numbered works of a composer.

clue.text: Study of people from North misrepresented in sorry statement

indicators.note: in places the jumbled compass word inside the statement

parts.note: an apology is a statement of being sorry

indicators.note: something misrepresented is presented wrongly, so its letters come out in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Northerners, having been misrepresented, receive an official apology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study of people' reads as a sociological survey of the North; North is really just letters to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropology is the academic discipline concerned with humankind, its societies and cultures.

clue.text: Biography with some text that's appropriate for killer

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: what is appropriate for a killer

parts.note: a biography is a life, as in Lives of the Poets
a sentence is a piece of text

explanation.surface: A biography containing a passage that suits a murderer's story.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as an adjective, but it describes the punishment a court sees fit for a murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A life sentence is the prison term for murder in Britain, the penalty a killer receives.

clue.text: Said bad things about male in regular row

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
things set in an even row are aligned

explanation.surface: A man criticised in a routine argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign someone is to speak ill of them, so maligned is a past-tense verb for badmouthed.

clue.text: Philistine's opponent, great French painter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the young Israelite who slew the Philistine giant Goliath
second meaning: Jacques-Louis, the neoclassical painter of The Death of Marat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Philistine' suggests someone who scorns art, setting up a contrast with the painter, but here it is Goliath's people.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical shepherd boy fought Goliath, and Jacques-Louis of the same surname was a leading French neoclassical artist.

clue.text: Expedition initially seeking a distant island

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of seeking
taken as written
far means distant
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An expedition at first in search of a remote island.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland trip, especially in Africa, to observe or hunt wild animals.

clue.text: Distress, we hear, that may stop runner

definitions.note: describes the word rather than standing in for it

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: woe is grief or distress

explanation.surface: Something distressing, it seems, that might halt a runner.
explanation.walkthrough: The runner is a horse, which a rider halts with this call.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the command shouted to make a horse stop or slow down.

clue.text: Irish writer putting in evergreen that quickly spreads

definitions.note: describes the noun: a fire that spreads quickly

indicators.note: the writer is putting the tree in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Dublin-born playwright
a fir is an evergreen conifer

explanation.surface: An Irish author planting an evergreen that grows fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish writer' could be Joyce, Shaw or Yeats; only Oscar Wilde's surname has room for the tree before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildfire is an uncontrolled blaze in countryside, proverbial for how rapidly it spreads.

clue.text: Woeful accommodation in hotel needing change of heart

indicators.note: heart is the middle letter, and changing it means swapping that one letter for another

parts.note: taken as written; its middle letter is to be replaced

explanation.surface: Dreadful lodgings at a hotel that needs a change of attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle T of HOTEL becomes V; the clue does not say which letter comes in, so the definition decides it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a squalid, wretched dwelling, so woeful accommodation.

clue.text: Husband and I beat impediment

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written
taken as written
to cap is to top or outdo

explanation.surface: A married couple overcoming an obstacle together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like a verb acting on the impediment, but it simply gives a synonym, cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a disadvantage or hindrance that makes progress harder.

clue.text: Be moved by bark from spaniel, oddly

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third, fifth and seventh letters are kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of spaniel

explanation.surface: Someone startled by a spaniel's bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bark' is a dog's noise in the surface, but it is a sailing ship (also spelt barque).
explanation.definitionFit: To sail is to travel on water by ship, and a bark is a type of sailing vessel.

clue.text: Put in grave situation with very limited area left in gap

parts.note: to inter is to place a body in a grave
very cut short to its abbreviation V
A is the abbreviation for area
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone placed in a serious predicament with little space left in a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave situation' reads as a crisis, but it is literally a position in a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a space or pause between two things, in time or distance.

clue.text: Host, say, protected by brave person

indicators.note: something protected by a guard is surrounded by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a brave person is lion-hearted, a lion
e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: A party host, as it were, shielded by a courageous guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like the person giving a party, but it means a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great number, an army, and so is a legion, as in 'their name is legion'.

clue.text: Certain extract from bulletin, if edited the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means back to front, so the run is read right to left
an extract is a passage lifted out, so the answer is a run of consecutive letters in the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of bulletin, all of if and the start of edited

explanation.surface: A sure piece taken from a news bulletin that was edited badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If edited' tempts an anagram, but the letters are only read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Definite means certain, beyond doubt or clearly fixed.

clue.text: Religious celebration at centre of belief I establish

indicators.note: at the centre of means lying inside, so the answer sits within the consecutive letters of the phrase

parts.note: the run of letters from the end of belief, the I and the start of establish

explanation.surface: A religious feast that lies at the heart of the faith someone founds.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta, in Spanish-speaking countries, is a festival, often held on a saint's day.

clue.text: Perfectionist almost ruined first illustration in book

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so its letters are scattered and rebuilt
almost means not quite all, so the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, losing its final letter before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A perfectionist nearly spoiled the first picture in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontispiece is the decorative picture facing a book's title page.

clue.text: Art of a kind, works primarily timeless

indicators.note: primarily means at the start, and timeless means without the time letter, so the leading T goes

parts.note: toils means labours, works

explanation.surface: Artworks, mostly ageless, of a particular kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily timeless' says the T at the start goes: it is without its leading time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oils are paintings done in oil paint, one kind of fine art.

clue.text: Substance that's hard found at bottom of mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A hard material discovered at the base of a mineshaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found at bottom of' places the H beneath PIT, which in a down clue means after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pith is the essential core or substance of something, as in the pith of an argument.

clue.text: Vehicle returned before end of warranty for service

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: end of means only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of warranty

explanation.surface: A vehicle taken back to the garage before its warranty runs out, for a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like car maintenance, but it is one of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: The navy is the seagoing branch of the armed services.

clue.text: Material about a Mediterranean area

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the Levant is the eastern Mediterranean coast

explanation.surface: Fabric or information concerning part of the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like a noun for cloth, but it is the adjective meaning pertinent.
explanation.definitionFit: Material evidence is relevant evidence: both mean pertinent to the matter at hand.

clue.text: With passion, they lead astray

indicators.note: led astray means off the right path, so the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Passionate people leading others into error.
explanation.definitionFit: Heatedly means in an angry or excited way, with strong feeling.
